sections.content: How many people are "other researchers, unspecified discipline"?

35,355 people

were counted on the census as "other researchers, unspecified discipline" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Other researchers, of unspecified discipline, perform research activities across a variety of disciplines for academic purposes or to provide the systematic investigation necessary for the development of new products and services, or to enhance the performance of existing ones.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "other researchers, unspecified discipline", 29.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other researchers, unspecified discipline" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other researchers, unspecified discipline" included:

  • web design professionals
  • actuaries, economists and statisticians
  • veterinarians

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "other researchers, unspecified discipline" there were a similar number of men and women (49.7% compared with 50.3%).

This means "other researchers, unspecified discipline" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 49.7% and women made up 50.3% of "other researchers, unspecified discipline"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other researchers, unspecified discipline" included:

  • insurance underwriters
  • database administrators and web content technicians
  • hotel and accommodation managers and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "other researchers, unspecified discipline" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "other researchers, unspecified discipline" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other researchers, unspecified discipline", 10% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (84.1% compared with 15.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.9%) than self-employed (2.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Oxford, this is in the region of the South East.
